notes: Round 2 re-check of both round-1 minors. T2 (bodies() projection) is closed correctly: bodies() now projects every component of ConsumerRecord (offset, timestampMillis) and every component of SegmentRecord (id, opType, version, payload), pinned by absolute literals on the inline arm. decodeInto only CONSTRUCTS offset and createdAt, and both are discriminated by the fixture -- createdAtMillis=11 from toByteArray(11L) is distinct from the per-record 7L passed to SegmentWriter.add and from 0, so reader.createdAtMillis()->0L reds; offset++ -> offset reds on 500/501/502. opType and version are constant across the fixture, so a constant-return mutation in SegmentReader.read would survive this class, but decodeInto passes SegmentRecord through by reference and the format-level round trip is pinned by SegmentReaderTest, GoldenSegmentTest and GoldenSegmentV1Test with OpType.DELETE. No fixture coupling introduced: the three arms use three separate CanPresign stores, hubs, bridges and clients, and the absolute-literal anchor sits on one arm with isEqualTo on the other two, which is the right shape.

T1 (url binding) verified as delegated rather than dropped. All four classes the new javadoc names exist and hold what it says: DirectFetchTest.ServesOneUrl serves one url and throws for any other with the observed url asserted equal to the minted one; DirectServingTest pins theGrantNamesTheSegmentBeingSERVED, theTTLIsCLAMPEDToSixtySecondsMeasuredFromTheEPOCH, aBATCHEDDeltaGrantsEachSegmentItsOWNKey and theGrantReachesNOLogLine; GrantIssuerTest and GrantNeverLoggedTest are present.

The move to plugin does not change what the bridge hands the consumer. HubBridge passes push.key/segmentKey/recordCount/firstOffset/via/segment/grant straight through to Delivery, the same shape as EndToEndTest.HubTransport plus the grant component that direct requires. plugin/build.gradle.kts already carries api(client), testImplementation(ingest) and testImplementation(binstore-backends), so the commit needs no build change and nothing in http is staged.

Mode pinning is load-bearing and per case: containsOnly(expected) on the modes read off the pushes kills coldMode reverting to a forced PROXY (direct arm) and kills a hub that inlines cold bytes (proxy arm). Criterion 2's test pins that the CONSUMER count, not the run count, reaches FetchPolicy: at two consumers and threshold 1 a hub passing 1 or committed.runs().size() would serve DIRECT and trip the AssertionError source. The <= boundary at fanOut == threshold is not exercised here but is pinned by FetchPolicyTest.theDIRECTFanOutThresholdIsCONFIGURATION at fan-out 8 against threshold 8.

One mutation survives this class and is killed elsewhere, so it is not raised as a finding: publishSegment adding a run twice per subscriber yields two deliveries and six records; recordsThrough reads exactly three and never asserts the stream is exhausted, and modesSeen=[INLINE,INLINE] still satisfies containsOnly. AssembledServingPathTest's containsExactly(FetchMode.INLINE) kills it.

testing.md: no Thread.sleep, no fixed port, no system temp, fakes rather than mocks. The 200 ms readNext timeout is never reached on the green path -- hub.publish is synchronous on the test thread and fills the queue before the first poll -- so it is a failure bound rather than a wait. Tier T1 (MemoryBinStore) is right: proxy and direct genuinely need a store to read through. Criterion 3 (ADR-0023) needs no new test: client declares only api(project(":format")), so an import of binjava.binstore in client/src/main cannot compile -- rung 1, not a prose claim.

Red records for both methods exist at the new path against the staged test bytes (sha 914da02ada48f3818f81a6293e6c26776058e1915417878c494e0e5bbc9ae2cc, matching git show :plugin/.../ThreeModesAgreeTest.java). No existing assertion was weakened: the only other staged file is backlog.md.
